text:
olivia: Quick sync — we need a short cost-utility matrix for the new 11B-int6 candidate to hand off to product/GTN. One pager w/ the numbers product cares about: p95 latency, mean latency, tokens/USD, and estimated quality delta vs baseline. Can someone post a compact summary + recommendation?

sanjay: TL;DR up front: ship as a gated hybrid route (default int6, fallback to int8 for high-value queries). Tradeoff looks good for chat and short-completion workloads. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

maya: adding numbers from the microbench and slice tests. kept it minimal.
```
model: nova11B-int6
slice: multi-turn chat (avg len 120 tok)
mean latency: 195ms
p95 latency: 420ms
cost/token (inference only): $0.00085
quality (ROUGE/QA proxy): -1.8% vs prod-13B-int8 (small drop on longform recall)

notes: latency tail increases on KV-cache coldstarts, but autoscaling handles steady-surge.
```

kevin: to add — product cares about UX risk. That -1.8% is concentrated in long-context recall slices (few prompts). For short chat turns (~<40 tokens) quality delta is ~-0.4% and cheaper by ~35% token-cost.

nora: from GTN perspective, key asks are: 1) single-line recommendation for deployment, 2) fast fallback plan if regressions observed, 3) a small AB test plan. Suggested phrasing: "Recommend hybrid default->int6 with 10% canary and deterministic fallback to int8 for low-confidence outputs."

olivia: perfect. Can we convert that into a 1-paragraph product-ready blurb + a 3-row cost-utility matrix?

sanjay: here's my attempt — short and actionable.
```
Product blurb: "We recommend rolling out nova11B-int6 as the default inference model for chat and short-completion flows to reduce token cost by ~35% while maintaining near-parity on user-facing quality. For long-form recall and high-stakes prompts, enable an int8 fallback or route to a higher-fidelity model. Start with a 10% canary and monitor recall signals and NPS-affecting slices; revert automatically if recall drops exceed 3% on the control set."

Cost-utility matrix (3 rows):
- Default (int6): cost/token $0.00085, mean latency 195ms, p95 420ms, quality delta -0.4% (short). Good for chat.
- Fallback (int8): cost/token $0.00130, mean latency 240ms, p95 480ms, quality delta baseline (0%). Use for low-confidence / long-recall.
- Conservative route (dedicated 13B): cost/token $0.0025, mean latency 360ms, p95 700ms, quality +1.2% but high cost. Use for critical tasks only.
```

maya: added the monitoring hooks to detect regressions: recall_score, hallucination_rate, and top-1 token divergence. Eval-bot will post slice alerts to #eng-ml when thresholds breach.

eval-bot: [alert-config] monitoring hooks created: recall_score (window=1h, threshold=-3%), hallucination_rate (>2%), top1_divergence (>5%). Posting alerts to #eng-ml and to the product runbook channel.

kevin: actionable next steps: 1) create canary config (10% traffic) with deterministic fallback, 2) add per-route latency budget (p95 < 500ms), 3) run 48h AB with N=10k sessions and evaluate recall + CSAT proxies. I'll draft the canary JSON and policy.

olivia: awesome. Can you paste that canary JSON here when done? Also add the experiment hypothesis one-liner for GTN: "Default int6 will reduce unit cost by ~35% w/ <1% negative impact on short-turn satisfaction; we expect recall regressions concentrated in 5% of long-context traffic and mitigatable via fallback."

nora: copying into product handoff doc after kevin posts the JSON. This is exactly the concise output we needed. :rocket:
